name: Route One 4-4-2

slots.why: Kicks long to the target man, so kicking and throwing matter.
Support full-back provides width for the early crosses.

Central defender. Cover is the alternate, as is the No-Nonsense Centre-Back (Defend or Cover), who clears rather than passes: every pass goes long and early anyway. Only one centre-back may use Cover.

Central defender on the right. Cover is the alternate, as is the No-Nonsense Centre-Back (Defend or Cover), who clears rather than passes: every pass goes long and early anyway. Only one centre-back may use Cover.
Winger (Support) crosses early for the target man and second striker.
Defensive central midfielder wins the ball and passes it forward simply.
Ball-winning midfielder wins the second ball from the knock-downs.
Winger (Support) crosses early from the right.
Target Man (Attack) is the primary long-ball outlet: he competes aerially, pins the centre-backs and attacks early crosses while the second striker attacks knock-downs and space around him.
Advanced Forward runs onto the flick-ons. Poacher is the alternate.

description: A deliberately direct system that moves the ball forward early toward a physical target and runners attacking second balls.
whyGood: The Target Man gives direct balls a reliable destination, the Advanced Forward attacks the space and second balls around him, and the midfield is selected to compete aggressively for loose balls. The system avoids asking weak technical players to build through pressure.
whyThisShape: A direct 4-4-2 that deliberately bypasses midfield pressure: long balls are aimed at a physical Target Man, the second striker attacks the knock-down or space beyond, and the wingers deliver early. The CM(D) holds the centre while the BWM attacks second balls.
whenToUse: When you have a big target man and a quick second striker, but weak technical midfielders; or against teams with small defenders.
whenNotToUse: Against tall, strong centre-backs who win the aerial duels, or when your squad is technical and would waste its passing.

instructionRationale.Much More Direct Passing: Deliberately bypass midfield pressure toward the target and second-ball runners.
instructionRationale.Higher Tempo: Move the ball before the opponent resets, using the receivers and runners supplied by the roles.
instructionRationale.Pass Into Space: Lead the mobile forwards and midfield runners into space rather than requiring every pass to arrive at their feet.
instructionRationale.Hit Early Crosses: Deliver before the defensive line resets, using the target or forward runners already attacking the box.
instructionRationale.Counter: Use the forward runners immediately after a regain, before the opponent can recover its shape.
instructionRationale.Regroup: Recover the defensive shape after losing possession; this is a positioning choice, not a measured guarantee about stamina or defensive success.
instructionRationale.Distribute Quickly: Release the forward outlets before the opponent recovers.
instructionRationale.Distribute To Target Man: The selected outlets match where this tactic starts its build-up or releases pressure.
instructionRationale.Fairly Wide: Give the wide outlets space to receive and stretch the opponent without isolating every central passer.
instructionRationale.Floated Crosses: A starting delivery choice for the receiving roles, to review against the actual forwards.
instructionRationale.Never Time Wasting: The kick-off baseline; review deliberately when score and time justify a different policy.
instructionRationale.Standard Defensive Line: Keep the back line at its mentality-relative default rather than explicitly pushing it up or dropping it.
instructionRationale.Standard Line of Engagement: Defend from a middle block; the forward roles still determine which players challenge the ball.
instructionRationale.Take Long Kicks: Use the selected forward or wide outlets without demanding short build-up under pressure.

keyRequirements: A genuinely dominant aerial Target Man who can make long distribution repeatable rather than hopeful
A fast or exceptionally well-timed second striker who attacks knock-downs and the space beyond
A BWM who aggressively competes for second balls while the CM(D) protects the centre
Wide players with reliable early delivery
A goalkeeper with adequate kicking to reach the intended outlet consistently
setupNotes: All three phases have been reviewed. Standard sliders are relative to the chosen mentality; unselected toggles intentionally leave FM to choose the response.
Player instructions use the selected role and duty defaults unless additional instructions are listed. Crossing and overlap settings are starting choices to review against the selected players.
